overnight.name: Overnight fund
overnight.summary: Lends money for just one day at a time, rolling it over every day.
overnight.watchOut: Grows very slowly; often just below what money-market rates pay.

liquid.name: Liquid fund
liquid.summary: Holds very short-term debt that matures within 91 days.
liquid.watchOut: Not a savings account: the value can dip slightly if a borrower defaults.

ultra-short-duration.name: Ultra short duration fund
ultra-short-duration.summary: Holds debt whose average duration is 3 to 6 months.
ultra-short-duration.watchOut: A little more sensitive to interest-rate changes than a liquid fund.

low-duration.name: Low duration fund
low-duration.summary: Holds debt whose average duration is 6 to 12 months.
low-duration.watchOut: Value moves a little when interest rates change.

money-market.name: Money market fund
money-market.summary: Holds money-market instruments that mature within one year, such as treasury bills and certificates of deposit.
money-market.watchOut: Returns follow short-term interest rates, which change over time.

short-duration.name: Short duration fund
short-duration.summary: Holds bonds whose average duration is 1 to 3 years.
short-duration.watchOut: When interest rates rise, the value of its bonds falls for a while.

short-and-mid-term.name: Short and mid term fund
short-and-mid-term.summary: A platform label rather than a SEBI category: debt funds holding bonds of roughly short to medium duration.
short-and-mid-term.watchOut: Check which SEBI category the fund actually belongs to.

medium-duration.name: Medium duration fund
medium-duration.summary: Holds bonds whose average duration is 3 to 4 years.
medium-duration.watchOut: More sensitive to interest-rate changes than short duration funds.

medium-to-long-duration.name: Medium to long duration fund
medium-to-long-duration.summary: Holds bonds whose average duration is 4 to 7 years.
medium-to-long-duration.watchOut: Its value can swing noticeably when interest rates change.

long-duration.name: Long duration fund
long-duration.summary: Holds bonds whose average duration is more than 7 years.
long-duration.watchOut: The most sensitive debt fund to interest-rate changes; it can fall for long stretches.

dynamic-bond.name: Dynamic bond fund
dynamic-bond.summary: Moves between short and long bonds depending on where the manager thinks interest rates are heading.
dynamic-bond.watchOut: Depends on the manager's calls about interest rates, which can be wrong.

corporate-bond.name: Corporate bond fund
corporate-bond.summary: Puts at least 80% in company bonds with the highest credit ratings (AA+ and above).
corporate-bond.watchOut: Even highly rated companies can be downgraded.

credit-risk.name: Credit risk fund
credit-risk.summary: Puts at least 65% in company bonds rated below the highest grades, which pay more interest.
credit-risk.watchOut: Higher interest comes with a higher chance a borrower doesn't pay back.

banking-and-psu.name: Banking and PSU debt fund
banking-and-psu.summary: Puts at least 80% in bonds of banks, public sector companies and public financial institutions.
banking-and-psu.watchOut: Still carries interest-rate risk and some credit risk.

gilt.name: Gilt fund
gilt.summary: Puts at least 80% in government securities, so the government is the borrower.
gilt.watchOut: Very low default risk, but prices still swing when interest rates change.

gilt-10-year-constant-maturity.name: Gilt fund with 10-year constant maturity
gilt-10-year-constant-maturity.summary: Puts at least 80% in government securities, keeping the portfolio's duration at about 10 years.
gilt-10-year-constant-maturity.watchOut: Long duration, so strongly affected by interest-rate changes.

floater.name: Floater fund
floater.summary: Puts at least 65% in bonds whose interest rate resets as market rates change.
floater.watchOut: Returns fall when interest rates fall.

index-debt.name: Debt index fund
index-debt.summary: Copies a bond index instead of picking bonds; some hold bonds until a fixed maturity date.
index-debt.watchOut: Prices still move with interest rates before maturity.

arbitrage.name: Arbitrage fund
arbitrage.summary: Buys a share in the cash market and sells it in the futures market at the same time, earning the small price gap. At least 65% is in shares, but hedged.
arbitrage.watchOut: Returns depend on how big those price gaps are, which changes with market conditions.

equity-savings.name: Equity savings fund
equity-savings.summary: Mixes shares (partly hedged with arbitrage) and at least 10% debt.
equity-savings.watchOut: The unhedged share portion can still fall.

conservative-hybrid.name: Conservative hybrid fund
conservative-hybrid.summary: Holds mostly debt (75–90%) with a small share portion (10–25%).
conservative-hybrid.watchOut: The share portion can still pull the value down in a market fall.

balanced-advantage.name: Balanced advantage fund
balanced-advantage.summary: Shifts between shares and debt, anywhere from 0 to 100%, based on the fund's own rules or market levels.
balanced-advantage.watchOut: How it behaves depends on the fund's model; two such funds can be very different.

dynamic-asset-allocation.name: Dynamic asset allocation fund
dynamic-asset-allocation.summary: The same SEBI category as balanced advantage: it moves between shares and debt anywhere from 0 to 100%.
dynamic-asset-allocation.watchOut: Read what rules the fund follows; the name alone doesn't say.

aggressive-hybrid.name: Aggressive hybrid fund
aggressive-hybrid.summary: Holds 65–80% in shares and 20–35% in debt.
aggressive-hybrid.watchOut: Mostly shares, so it can fall sharply in a crash.

balanced-hybrid.name: Balanced hybrid fund
balanced-hybrid.summary: Holds 40–60% in shares and 40–60% in debt, without arbitrage.
balanced-hybrid.watchOut: Half in shares means real ups and downs.

multi-asset-allocation.name: Multi asset allocation fund
multi-asset-allocation.summary: Holds at least three asset classes, such as shares, debt and gold, with at least 10% in each.
multi-asset-allocation.watchOut: Spreading out lowers risk but doesn't remove it.

sif.name: Specialised investment fund (SIF)
sif.summary: A newer SEBI product between mutual funds and portfolio management, for investors putting in at least ₹10 lakh. It can use strategies normal funds can't, such as limited short selling.
sif.watchOut: Not a regular mutual fund: higher minimums and more complex strategies.

large-cap.name: Large cap fund
large-cap.summary: Puts at least 80% in the 100 largest listed companies by market value.
large-cap.watchOut: Big companies still fall in a crash.

large-and-mid-cap.name: Large and mid cap fund
large-and-mid-cap.summary: Puts at least 35% in large companies (top 100) and at least 35% in mid-sized ones (101st to 250th).
large-and-mid-cap.watchOut: Mid-sized companies swing more than large ones.

elss.name: ELSS (tax saver) fund
elss.summary: Puts at least 80% in shares and locks money in for 3 years. Under the old tax regime, money put in can reduce taxable income.
elss.watchOut: You can't take the money out for 3 years, even in an emergency.

multi-cap.name: Multi cap fund
multi-cap.summary: Puts at least 25% each in large, mid-sized and small companies.
multi-cap.watchOut: The fixed small-company share adds swings.

flexi-cap.name: Flexi cap fund
flexi-cap.summary: Puts at least 65% in shares of any size, in any mix the manager chooses.
flexi-cap.watchOut: The mix depends on the manager's choices.

focused.name: Focused fund
focused.watchOut: Fewer holdings means one bad pick hurts more.

value.name: Value fund
value.summary: Picks shares that look cheap compared with what the company earns or owns.
value.watchOut: Cheap shares can stay cheap for years.

contra.name: Contra fund
contra.summary: Buys shares that are currently out of favour, betting against the crowd.
contra.watchOut: Going against the crowd can mean waiting a long time, or being wrong.

mid-cap.name: Mid cap fund
mid-cap.summary: Puts at least 65% in mid-sized companies (101st to 250th by market value).
mid-cap.watchOut: Swings more than large cap funds in both directions.

small-cap.name: Small cap fund
small-cap.summary: Puts at least 65% in small companies (251st onwards by market value).
small-cap.watchOut: Can fall very sharply and take years to recover.

dividend-yield.name: Dividend yield fund
dividend-yield.summary: Puts at least 65% in shares of companies that pay out a good part of their profits as dividends.
dividend-yield.watchOut: Dividends can be cut, and share prices still fall.

index-nifty-50.name: Nifty 50 index fund
index-nifty-50.summary: Copies the Nifty 50: the 50 large companies in the NSE's main index, in the same proportions.
index-nifty-50.watchOut: Falls with the whole market; there's no manager trying to avoid it.

index-nifty-next-50.name: Nifty Next 50 index fund
index-nifty-next-50.summary: Copies the Nifty Next 50: the 50 companies ranked just after the Nifty 50.

index-sensex.name: Sensex index fund
index-sensex.summary: Copies the Sensex: 30 large companies listed on the BSE.
index-sensex.watchOut: Only 30 companies, so a few big ones move it a lot.

index-others.name: Other index funds
index-others.summary: Copy other indices, such as mid cap, small cap, sector or strategy indices.
index-others.watchOut: Risk depends on the index it copies.

etf-index.name: Index ETF
etf-index.summary: Copies an index like an index fund, but is bought and sold on the stock exchange during the day, like a share.
etf-index.watchOut: Needs a demat account, and the trading price can differ slightly from the fund's value.

gold-etf.name: Gold ETF
gold-etf.summary: Tracks the price of gold in India and is backed by physical gold, traded on the stock exchange.
gold-etf.watchOut: Gold prices can fall and stay flat for years.

etf-others.name: Other ETFs
etf-others.summary: Exchange-traded funds that track silver, bonds, sectors or other indices.
etf-others.watchOut: Risk depends on what it tracks.

sector-banking-financial-services.name: Banking and financial services fund
sector-banking-financial-services.summary: Puts at least 80% in banks, lenders, insurers and other financial companies.
sector-banking-financial-services.watchOut: One sector means one bad patch for that sector hits the whole fund.

sector-infrastructure.name: Infrastructure fund
sector-infrastructure.summary: Puts at least 80% in companies building roads, power, ports, construction and similar.
sector-infrastructure.watchOut: Depends heavily on government spending and interest rates.

sector-auto.name: Auto fund
sector-auto.summary: Puts at least 80% in vehicle makers and their parts suppliers.
sector-auto.watchOut: Tied to how many vehicles people buy.

sector-energy-and-power.name: Energy and power fund
sector-energy-and-power.summary: Puts at least 80% in oil, gas, power and other energy companies.
sector-energy-and-power.watchOut: Moves with fuel prices and government rules.

sector-pharma.name: Pharma and healthcare fund
sector-pharma.summary: Puts at least 80% in medicine makers, hospitals and healthcare companies.
sector-pharma.watchOut: Tied to one industry's regulations and exports.

sector-consumption.name: Consumption fund
sector-consumption.summary: Puts at least 80% in companies selling everyday goods and services to households.
sector-consumption.watchOut: Depends on how much people spend.

sector-services.name: Services fund
sector-services.summary: Puts at least 80% in service companies, such as finance, telecom and logistics.
sector-services.watchOut: Concentrated in one part of the economy.

sector-technology.name: Technology fund
sector-technology.summary: Puts at least 80% in software, IT services and tech companies.
sector-technology.watchOut: Can rise and fall sharply with global tech spending.

thematic-global.name: Global fund
thematic-global.summary: Invests in companies listed outside India.
thematic-global.watchOut: Adds currency risk: the rupee's value changes returns.

thematic-mnc.name: MNC fund
thematic-mnc.summary: Invests in Indian-listed companies whose parent is a multinational.
thematic-mnc.watchOut: Concentrated in one style of company.

thematic-others.name: Other thematic funds
thematic-others.summary: Follow a theme across sectors, such as manufacturing, ESG or defence.
thematic-others.watchOut: Themes go in and out of fashion.

fof-domestic.name: Fund of funds (domestic)
fof-domestic.summary: Invests in other Indian mutual funds instead of buying shares or bonds directly.
fof-domestic.watchOut: Two layers of costs, and risk depends on the funds it holds.

fof-overseas.name: Fund of funds (overseas)
fof-overseas.summary: Invests in mutual funds or ETFs abroad.
fof-overseas.watchOut: Currency risk, plus limits on how much Indian funds may invest overseas.

fof-others.name: Other funds of funds
fof-others.summary: Funds of funds that don't fit the domestic or overseas groups.
fof-others.watchOut: Check what the underlying funds hold.

solution-childrens.name: Children's fund
solution-childrens.summary: Built around a child's future, with a lock-in of at least 5 years or until the child turns 18, whichever comes first.
solution-childrens.watchOut: The lock-in means the money isn't available for emergencies.

solution-retirement.name: Retirement fund
solution-retirement.summary: Built for retirement, with a lock-in of at least 5 years or until retirement age, whichever comes first.
solution-retirement.watchOut: The lock-in means the money isn't available for emergencies.
